source.title: ICCU: In-Context Continual Unlearning via Pattern-Induced Refusal Rules

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether ICCU, a different in-context rule-based method, maintains refusal behavior under paraphrased, translated, and jailbreak-wrapped queries. It does not test recovery attacks on parameter-unlearned models.
record.gate_note: The robustness experiments evaluate ICCU’s filter refusal rate, not whether answers reveal recovered knowledge. The filter mode does not generate answers in the reported robustness evaluation. Results for GA, NPO, RMU, LUNAR, and O3 are comparisons in other experiments, not attack-recovery tests. Guardrail Classifier robustness results are not included as rows because these rows record ICCU’s counter-method results.
record.test_reason: ICCU is a newer, parameter-free unlearning method. The study reports how its refusal holds up under prompt-only attacks: TOFU paraphrases, six machine translations, and DAN and ignore-instructions jailbreaks. That bears on version F's claim of resisting such attacks. Two caveats apply. The measure is the filter's refusal decision, not whether attacked prompts recover the forgotten knowledge. The method by design leaves the knowledge in the weights.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that ICCU keeps high forget-side refusal and low retain-side refusal under paraphrase, translation and two jailbreak wrappers. They attribute higher Chinese retain refusal to embedding entanglement. In the Limitations they concede that ICCU suppresses rather than erases knowledge, which stays in the weights. The robustness claims rest only on Llama-3-8B-Instruct on TOFU in filter mode.
record.recipe_differences: ICCU induces and retrieves natural-language refusal rules at inference time without modifying parameters; the paper does not apply the original parameter-unlearning methods in attack-recovery tests.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome depends on query language: Chinese translations show notably higher retain-side refusal. Russian retain-side rates also rise relative to the original-query baseline in some splits.
record.problems: The robustness metric is refusal rate, not answer accuracy or recovery of targeted knowledge. The filter-based robustness evaluation does not generate answers. Prompt-attack robustness is reported for Llama-3-8B-Instruct; broader model coverage is not reported for these attacks.
record.rows_left_out: No ICCU robustness results from Tables 4, 5, or 11 were left out. Comparator Guardrail Classifier values were omitted. Other baseline unlearning results were not attack-recovery evaluations.

untested.parts: No parameter-unlearned model is attacked. Baseline GA/NPO/RMU/LUNAR/O3 accuracies are reported without any recovery attack.
No relearning or fine-tuning attack on any method.
No activation ablation or probing. The authors only state that ICCU leaves knowledge in the weights.
Prompt attacks are not measured as recovery of knowledge from parameter-unlearned models.

Prompt attacks are tested only on Llama-3-8B-Instruct with TOFU in filter mode. Untested: Llama-2-7B, Qwen3-14B, WMDP, and end-to-end mode under attack. Also untested: adaptive attacks aimed at the filter or embedding gate, in-context or multi-turn attacks, and fine-tuning, activation-edit or quantization attacks. Recovery of knowledge in generated answers is not measured.

record.verdict_notes: Refusal rate here is the gate-plus-classifier decision, so 'resisting' prompt attacks means the filter still flags the query. Answers to attacked prompts are not checked for leaked knowledge. The jailbreaks are generic wrappers, not adaptive attacks on the filter. Because knowledge stays in the weights, ICCU makes no robustness claim against weight-level attacks (B, C, D); the authors say parameter methods are recoverable but do not test it. R43–R48 duplicate Table 2 baselines.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test simple attacks on parameter-unlearned models or whether such attacks recover targeted knowledge after accuracy is brought near chance.
No fine-tuning or relearning attack is applied after unlearning.

No activation-direction ablation or empirical recovery assay. The authors state that ICCU leaves model parameters unchanged and uses an external rule layer, but do not test recovery of knowledge from parameter-unlearned models.
Prompt variants are tested for ICCU refusal robustness, but the study does not measure whether those prompts restore answers or targeted knowledge.

Tests paraphrasing, several translated query sets, and two jailbreak wrappers against ICCU’s filter. Does not test resistance to fine-tuning, activation edits, quantization, or attacks against parameter-updated unlearning methods.

relation.reason: The paper reports its own robustness results under paraphrase, six translations and two jailbreak wrappers (Tables 4, 5, 11).

tranche.reason: ICCU is a different, parameter-free counter-method tested against prompt-only attacks (paraphrase, translation, jailbreak wrappers), which bears on version F.

source_check.notes: The DAN and ignore-instructions templates (App. J) are quoted attack prompts. TOFU filter mode uses an off-the-shelf Llama-3-8B-Instruct that never learned TOFU, so refusal rates measure only the filter, not knowledge recovery. Tables 4 and 11 do not name the model; Llama-3-8B-Instruct is inferred from Sec. 5 and the Table 5 baselines. ICCU suppresses rather than erases (Limitations). R19 must read 1.000.

statements.correction: ICCU (Llama-3-8B-Instruct, TOFU, filter mode): Chinese-translated retain refusal 0.323/0.300/0.277 vs 0.075/0.039/0.006 on original queries (Tables 11, 2). This is benign over-refusal, not an MMLU or utility drop. Paraphrase, French, Portuguese, Spanish, Italian and both jailbreaks stay within about 0.02 of baseline; Russian rises about 0.04-0.05.
statements.problem: Cites ICCU rows R38, R40, R42 under a capability-cost claim but never names ICCU. Its listed measures (MMLU, MT-Bench, utility, retain accuracy) do not include ICCU's measure, which is retain-side refusal under Chinese translation only.

statements.correction: Retain refusal within about 0.03 of baseline under paraphrase, French, Portuguese, Spanish and Italian. Russian rises by +0.047, +0.044 and +0.043 (0.122, 0.083, 0.049). Chinese reaches 0.323, 0.300 and 0.277.
statements.problem: Chinese numbers are right. 'Within about 0.03 under European-language translations' fails for Russian, a European language whose rows (R20, R22) the statement itself cites: 0.122/0.083/0.049 vs 0.075/0.039/0.006.
